claims.text: A polycrystalline solid solution containing aligned SRO precipitates can be used for lattice heat conduction.
Aligned SRO precipitate morphology minimizes phonon scattering relative to random precipitate morphology.
Aligned SRO precipitates reduce the negative effect of precipitates on lattice thermal conductivity.
Controlled precipitation and annealing can introduce an aligned SRO precipitate morphology.
The temperature range 300–500 K minimizes phonon-phonon interactions.
The temperature range 300–500 K maximizes the effect of precipitate alignment on phonon scattering.
SRO precipitates with sizes of 10–50 nm are comparable to or smaller than the dominant phonon wavelengths.
Using SRO precipitates with sizes of 10–50 nm reduces phonon scattering.
SRO precipitate spacing of 100–500 nm reduces phonon scattering while maintaining a coherent precipitate-matrix interface.
A coherent precipitate-matrix interface enhances phonon transmission and reduces phonon reflection.
Enhanced transmission across a coherent precipitate-matrix interface increases phonon mean free path.
Aligning SRO precipitates minimizes the number of phonon-precipitate interactions.
Phonons can travel more freely along the precipitate-alignment direction.
Aligned precipitates provide a more ordered structure that allows phonons to retain coherence over longer distances.
Reduced phonon scattering increases phonon mean free path.
An increased phonon mean free path enhances lattice thermal conductivity.
Aligned SRO precipitates will increase lattice thermal conductivity by 10–20% relative to random SRO precipitates.
Phonon-transport models for nanostructured materials support a significant reduction in scattering rates from aligned precipitates.
The proposed effect applies for precipitate volume fractions of 0.01–0.1.
The proposed effect applies for matrix grain sizes of 1–10 μm.
